comments.author: hbn
comments.story: Google Broke Image Search for Creative Commons
comments.why: Demonstrates Google confidently giving a wrong invention date for the touch lamp.
comments.text: There's also something to be said about how Google should be returning information, not answers. Skip to the 1:00 mark in this Technology Connections video where he demonstrates how if you ask Google when the touch lamp was invented it'll pop up with a giant, confident answer of 1984, despite the fact that if you do the research yourself you can find the first patent for it was filed in 1954. comments.author: slipframe
comments.story: Google turned me into a serial killer
comments.why: Shows Google's knowledge graph taking internet claims at face value.
comments.text: Technology Connections had a great observation about this in his video about touch lamps: the problem with Google's knowledge graph is that it takes everything it reads on the internet at face value. [VIDEO] (0:58 through 4:20)

comments.author: BrazzVuvuzela
comments.text: Taking google's answer for things they're calculating with math is probably safe, but if you get into the habit of reading google's answers to queries it will have you believing a lot of nonsense because many of the answers google offers are not calculated at all, but instead are regurgitated nonsense that google read on the internet and took at face value (example from Technology Connections: [VIDEO] )
